message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they diverged from other carnivores early on. Their lineage split from the ursid (bear) family around 20–25 million years ago. Over time, they evolved specialized traits—such as a pseudo‑thumb and a diet heavily reliant on bamboo—to adapt to their forested habitats. This evolutionary path led to the modern giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), which is now classified within the subfamily Ailurinae.
